response_json.request: Add a sliding switch on the bottom to provide a convenient on and off function

parameters.switch_type: Two-position linear ON/OFF slide switch assembly
parameters.mounting_surface: Lower base shell of the main housing
parameters.placement: On the broad underside, approximately on the lateral centerline and longitudinally offset into the control-region half shown in the bottom multiview image
parameters.orientation: Align the switch travel axis with the enclosure longitudinal axis
parameters.slider_profile: Rounded oblong finger pad matching the switch slot
parameters.slot_length: Parameterize from the required ON/OFF travel plus end clearances
parameters.slot_width: Parameterize from the actuator neck width plus running clearance
parameters.slider_clearance: Provide uniform sliding clearance around the actuator neck and beneath the external finger pad
parameters.edge_treatment: Small chamfer or fillet around the slot and rounded external slider edges
parameters.positions: Two mechanically distinct end positions corresponding to OFF and ON

actions.target: the bottom of the existing model
actions.relational_constraint: The sliding switch must be located on the bottom. Place it on the broad lower base shell, approximately centered across the enclosure width and offset longitudinally as shown in the bottom view. Keep the switch travel parallel to the housing longitudinal direction, maintain clearance from the blended perimeter and end-cap transitions, and verify internal clearance from the wheel-support pedestal and thumb-wheel mechanism.
actions.unresolved_reference: Resolved: the bottom is the Lower base shell in section S01, face_code 0002, Brep_id FACE 9. Exact switch dimensions, travel, wall thickness, and internal electrical component envelope remain unspecified and must be defined as design parameters or matched to a selected commercial switch.
steps: Activate section S01, Main streamlined housing, and select the Lower base shell identified by face_code 0002 and Brep_id FACE 9. Do not modify the upper crown, side flanks, end caps, wheel-support pedestal, or thumb wheel except where a clearance check requires a minor positional adjustment of the new switch.

Use the bottom multiview image to localize the switch on the broad central region of face 0002. Position the switch approximately on the enclosure lateral centerline and longitudinally offset into the same control-region half indicated by the image, while keeping adequate material between the opening and the perimeter blends.

Inspect the local curvature of face 0002. Because the lower base shell is a subtly shaped B-spline surface rather than a guaranteed planar face, create a datum plane tangent to the underside at the intended switch center. Orient one datum axis parallel to the STEP z-axis, which is the enclosure longitudinal direction.

Project the housing centerline, relevant perimeter edges, and the desired switch center onto the datum plane. Constrain the switch sketch symmetrically about the lateral centerline and dimension its longitudinal offset from a stable housing datum or end reference rather than from a freeform edge.

Create a parameterized sketch for the actuator opening. Use a center-to-center slot tool or a rectangle with semicircular ends to form a capsule-shaped profile. Constrain the long axis parallel to the enclosure longitudinal axis and size the profile from the required switch travel, actuator-neck width, and assembly clearances.

Map or project the slot profile onto face 0002 if required by the CAD system. Cut the slot normal to the datum plane using an Up to Next, Through Shell, or equivalent termination so that the opening penetrates the lower housing wall without unnecessarily cutting the opposite crown surface.

If the housing is represented as a solid without explicit shell thickness, establish the required enclosure wall thickness before detailing the switch seat. Create an inward offset of the local underside or use a controlled pocket depth that preserves a structurally adequate wall around the opening.

Create a shallow recessed mounting pocket on the interior side of face 0002 for the fixed switch body. Center it on the actuator slot and size it to the selected electrical slide-switch envelope, including assembly clearance and space for terminals or wiring.

Add internal guide or retention geometry as required. Create two parallel guide rails, snap tabs, screw bosses, or a retaining frame around the internal pocket so the fixed switch body cannot translate when the external slider is operated.

Create new section S04 as a separate sliding-switch assembly. On the underside tangent datum plane, sketch the external finger pad as a rounded oblong profile larger than the actuator slot so that it overlaps and conceals the opening in both end positions.

Extrude the finger pad outward from the underside by a low ergonomic height. Keep the projection shallow enough that it does not cause excessive rocking when the enclosure rests on a flat surface, but high enough to permit fingertip or thumbnail operation.

Add an actuator neck beneath the finger pad. Extrude the neck through the slot with uniform running clearance and connect it to the selected internal switch actuator or modeled carrier. Keep the external slider as a separate movable solid rather than fusing it to S01.

Round the exposed slider perimeter with fillets to produce the smooth oblong appearance visible in the bottom image. Apply a small chamfer or fillet to the housing slot rim to remove sharp edges and reduce wear during sliding.

Define the linear motion relation for S04. Constrain the slider laterally and normal to the underside while permitting translation only along the enclosure longitudinal axis. Limit travel between two endpoints corresponding to OFF and ON.

Add two detent features or interface the slider with the detents of the selected commercial switch. Verify that each endpoint provides a positive, stable state and that the slider cannot overtravel beyond the electrical actuator limits.

Perform an interference and clearance analysis against S01, S02, and S03. In particular, check the internal switch body and actuator against the central wheel-support pedestal and the thumb-wheel operating envelope. If interference exists, shift the switch minimally along the longitudinal centerline while preserving the bottom-view placement intent.

Check the bottom support envelope against a planar ground reference. Confirm that the switch pad does not become the primary support point when placed on a surface; recess the assembly further or reduce pad height if necessary.
Optionally add recessed ON and OFF markings adjacent to the two travel endpoints on face 0002. Orient the markings for readability from the bottom and keep them clear of the slot-edge fillet.

Finish by validating minimum wall thickness, edge distance, slider running clearance, end-stop strength, assembly access, and manufacturability. Retain S01 as the modified housing section and S04 as the newly created movable switch section.
